raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3551/files) against `main`.

Addresses #2541.

## What was broken

`softmax_type="learnable"` (the learnable attention sink) with `cp_comm_type="p2p"` was rejected by an assertion. Behind that assertion, the p2p fused-attention helpers never passed `softmax_type` to `fused_attn_fwd` / `fused_attn_bwd`, so the kernels fell back to `"vanilla"` and ignored `softmax_offset`.

## What changed

* `cp_p2p_fwd_fused_attn` / `cp_p2p_bwd_fused_attn` take `softmax_type` and `softmax_offset`. The offset joins the auxiliary tensor pack in the order the forward returns it (`[stats, rng, (bias), (offset)]`). The previously unconditional `attn_bias = rest[0]` is now guarded by whether a bias was passed, because with a sink the pack would otherwise return the offset as the bias.
* **The sink enters each query row's softmax exactly once.** cuDNN counts the sink as one more softmax column, so the softmax stats of a tile include `e^offset`. The p2p forward merges the tiles' stats, so passing the offset to every tile would add the sink once per tile that a row visits. Only step 0 gets the sink: it is the local KV tile, and it covers every local query row (the diagonal tile under a causal mask, the full tile without one). The other tiles run a plain softmax. In the backward, only the mirror tile passes the sink and returns its gradient. The other tiles' dq/dk/dv use the merged stats, which already include the sink.
* **Sink gradient reduction.** Each rank's sink gradient covers only its own query rows. It is all-reduced over the CP group, so every rank returns the full-sequence gradient. This matches the a2a path, which all-gathers the per-head gradients, and it is what `run_attention_with_cp.py` compares against.
* `utils.py` and `attn_forward_func_with_cp`: fused attention is no longer disabled for non-vanilla softmax with p2p. With a sink, the FP8 per-tile forward returns the offset as a third aux tensor, and the FP8 unpacking now accepts it. The existing gate for FP8 with a sink on sm < 100 or cuDNN < 9.21 still applies.
* Tests:
  * `test_attention_with_cp.py` now runs the non-vanilla softmax cases (`cp_4_1` off-by-one, `cp_4_2` learnable) for p2p as well as a2a.
  * `run_attention_with_cp.py` kept the reference sink gradient as an alias of `softmax_offset.grad`, then zeroed it before the CP run accumulated into the same tensor. The sink-gradient check therefore compared the CP result with itself, for a2a as well. It now clones the reference.
  * The learnable offsets are drawn as `randn * 5` from a fixed CPU generator. With the default zero offset, the sink is almost invisible next to thousands of keys.

An earlier version of this PR passed the sink to every tile and did not reduce the gradient. Both errors cancel without a mask at cp=2: every row was counted twice, and each rank held half the rows. Under a causal mask they don't cancel: the sum of the per-rank sink gradients was off by up to 0.84 (reference max 6.36). The CP test skipped non-vanilla softmax for p2p, and its sink-gradient check compared against an alias, so neither caught it.

## Verification

### GH200, cp=2

Two GH200 nodes (sm_90), one GPU each, cross-node over InfiniBand, cp=2, BF16, FusedAttention. The run used TE main `fac8d4a9` with this PR's Python files on top, cuDNN 9.24.0, and torch 2.14.1+cu130. `run_attention_with_cp.py` was run with the changes above:

| softmax | comm | layout | TE Python | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| learnable (`cp_4_2`) | p2p | bshd | this PR | pass |
| learnable (`cp_4_2`) | p2p | sbhd | this PR | pass |
| off-by-one (`cp_4_1`) | p2p | bshd | this PR | pass |
| vanilla (`cp_4_0`) | p2p | bshd | this PR | pass |
| learnable (`cp_4_2`) | a2a | bshd | main | pass |
| off-by-one (`cp_4_1`) | a2a | bshd | main | pass |
| learnable (`cp_4_2`) | p2p | bshd | previous PR head `649969bb` | **fail**: sink gradient, 12/64 heads, max abs diff 1.55 |

"pass" means out, dq, dk, dv and the sink gradient are all within the runner's tolerances. All configs are causal GQA with s=4096. The two a2a rows show that the runner changes keep the existing a2a cases passing.

Sink gradient, per rank, max abs diff against the non-CP reference (`cp_4_2`, offsets `randn * 5`):

| mask | reference max | previous PR head | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| causal | 6.36 | 0.84 (sum over ranks) | 0.0032 |
| no_mask | 2.55 | 0.51 (sum over ranks) | 0.0030 |

### B300 (sm_103), cp=2 and cp=4

The B300 run used TE main `fac8d4a9` built for `103a` with CUDA 13.3, with this PR's Python files on top, cuDNN 9.27.0 and torch 2.14.1+cu130.

| Run | Selection | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_attention_with_cp.py`, CI default (`NVTE_TEST_ESSENTIAL=1`) | `cp_4_2`, `cp_4_3`; p2p and a2a | 58 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_attention_with_cp.py`, `NVTE_TEST_ESSENTIAL=0` | `cp_4_1`, `cp_4_2`, `cp_4_3` × BF16/FP16 × bshd/sbhd/thd; p2p and a2a | 30 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_attention_with_cp.py`, FP8 | `cp_4_2`, p2p, delayed/current/MXFP8 scaling, sbhd/thd | 26 passed, 0 failed |
| Same FP8 selection, two-entry FP8 aux unpacking | | fails with "too many values to unpack (expected 2)" |
| `run_attention_with_cp.py` on 4 GPUs (cp=4), BF16 | p2p `cp_4_2` bshd/sbhd/thd, `cp_4_1`, `cp_4_0`; a2a `cp_4_2` | all pass |
| Same, previous PR head `649969bb` | p2p `cp_4_2` bshd | **fail**: sink gradient, 14–47 of 64 heads per rank, max abs diff 6.52 |

The essential run includes p2p with thd (cuDNN ≥ 9.26), and a2a with the new non-zero offsets for sbhd and thd, `cp_4_3` (sliding window) and FP8. The FP8 p2p cases are the FP8 change in this PR.

An FP64 emulation of the p2p tile schedule shows the same pattern. With the sink on every tile, the ratio of the CP sum to the reference ranges from 0.5× to 2× per head at cp=2, and from 0.25× to 4× at cp=4. With the sink on step 0 only, it matches to 1e-15 at both sizes.

## Not covered

* The flash-attention backend.
* FP8 with a sink on sm_90, where the existing FP8 + sink gate on sm < 100 keeps FusedAttention off.
* `cp_size > 4`, and the a2a runs at cp=4 beyond `cp_4_2` bshd.
* `cp_comm_type="a2a+p2p"`, which is still rejected for non-vanilla softmax.

## Question for reviewers

Both a2a and p2p now return the full-sequence sink gradient on every CP rank. Other parameters get only their own tokens' gradient on each CP rank. Megatron-LM scales the loss by the CP size and scales dense gradients by `1 / dp_cp_group.size()` before the DP×CP reduction. As far as I can tell, it treats `softmax_offset` like any other parameter. In that setup, the sink gradient would come out `cp_size` times larger than the weights' gradients. Is the full gradient on every rank the intended contract, or should both paths return the per-rank partial sum? I kept the existing a2a contract here so that the two paths agree.

nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The changes affect context\-parallel attention training that uses P2P communication\. The PR still needs the previously reported bias-gradient shape fix before merging.

Findings

1.  **Offset Corrupts Bias Gradient Shape** ▶

Summary

Adds learnable and off-by-one softmax support to P2P context parallelism. - P2P attention now supports learnable softmax sinks. Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Support FP8 attention with a sink in CP ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/2f77d8056bd608c0d5a285dfff68fefa82f02487) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

I pushed a correction to this PR: 462355ea ("Count the attention sink once per query row in CP p2p") and aa5a1771 (tests).

The earlier version was wrong. cuDNN counts the sink as one more softmax column, so it is included in every p2p tile's softmax stats. Passing the offset to every tile made the LSE merge count the sink once per tile that a query row visits. I also claimed that every rank already holds the full sink gradient. That is not true for p2p, where each rank computes only its own query rows. Without a mask at cp=2, the two errors cancel, which is what my original check measured. Under a causal mask they don't.

The sink now goes only to the local KV tile (step 0), and the sink gradient is all-reduced over the CP group to match a2a. The CP test now covers p2p for learnable and off-by-one softmax. It also fixes an aliased reference that made the sink-gradient check compare the CP result with itself. I updated the description with the cross-node GH200 results, and the updated test fails on the previous head.

There is one open question at the end of the description, about whether every CP rank should return the full sink gradient (the current a2a contract) or only its partial sum.

I pushed 2f77d805 ("Support FP8 attention with a sink in CP p2p") and updated the description with B300 (sm_103) results.

With a sink, the FP8 per-tile forward returns the offset as a third aux tensor. The FP8 branch unpacked exactly two entries, so I had kept FP8 + sink + p2p off FusedAttention. On B300 the FP8 cases fail with "too many values to unpack" when only that gate is removed. With the unpacking fixed they pass: delayed, current and MXFP8 scaling, sbhd and thd. So the commit fixes the unpacking and drops the gate.

The B300 runs also cover cases the GH200 runs did not:
- p2p with thd, on cuDNN 9.27
- BF16 and FP16 across all three layouts
- a2a with the new non-zero offsets, including the sliding-window config and FP8
- cp=4 on four GPUs

All pass. The previous head fails the sink-gradient check at cp=4 as well.

The question about the per-rank sink-gradient contract at the end of the description is still open.

**Sink Is Counted Per Tile** `softmax_offset` is passed unchanged to every fused P2P tile, and each fused call installs it as its own sink token. For `cp_size = N`, the generic LSE merge therefore includes `N * exp(offset)`, while the learnable-softmax contract appends only one global sink. Every `cp_size > 1` run consequently computes incorrect probabilities and accumulates the gradient of an N-sink operation instead of the intended single sink.

**FP8 Aux Unpacking Fails** This selector now admits FP8 learnable softmax with P2P on supported Blackwell and cuDNN configurations. In that path, fused attention returns `[stats, rng, offset]`, but the P2P helper still unpacks the auxiliary tensors as exactly `[stats, rng]`. The newly enabled configuration therefore raises a tuple-unpacking error immediately after the fused forward call.

nodes.body: **Offset Corrupts Bias Gradient Shape** With `post_scale_bias` and learnable softmax, P2P reconstructs the backward auxiliary pack as `[stats, rng, bias, offset]`. The fused backward binding allocates `dBias` using the shape of the last auxiliary tensor, which is now the `[1, h, 1, 1]` offset rather than the tile bias. This configuration cannot return a correctly shaped bias gradient and may fail backward shape validation.

A P2P regression using a meaningful nonzero offset should verify both the output and `d_softmax_offset`; otherwise the original silent fallback and the new tile-accumulation behavior can regress unnoticed. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

inline_comments.body: **Sink Is Counted Per Tile** `softmax_offset` is passed unchanged to every fused P2P tile, and each fused call installs it as its own sink token. For `cp_size = N`, the generic LSE merge therefore includes `N * exp(offset)`, while the learnable-softmax contract appends only one global sink. Every `cp_size > 1` run consequently computes incorrect probabilities and accumulates the gradient of an N-sink operation instead of the intended single sink.

**FP8 Aux Unpacking Fails** This selector now admits FP8 learnable softmax with P2P on supported Blackwell and cuDNN configurations. In that path, fused attention returns `[stats, rng, offset]`, but the P2P helper still unpacks the auxiliary tensors as exactly `[stats, rng]`. The newly enabled configuration therefore raises a tuple-unpacking error immediately after the fused forward call.

inline_comments.body: **Offset Corrupts Bias Gradient Shape** With `post_scale_bias` and learnable softmax, P2P reconstructs the backward auxiliary pack as `[stats, rng, bias, offset]`. The fused backward binding allocates `dBias` using the shape of the last auxiliary tensor, which is now the `[1, h, 1, 1]` offset rather than the tile bias. This configuration cannot return a correctly shaped bias gradient and may fail backward shape validation.

issue_comments.body:
Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The changes affect context\-parallel attention training that uses P2P communication\. The PR still needs the previously reported bias-gradient shape fix before merging.

Findings

1.  **Offset Corrupts Bias Gradient Shape** ▶

Summary

Adds learnable and off-by-one softmax support to P2P context parallelism. - P2P attention now supports learnable softmax sinks. Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Support FP8 attention with a sink in CP ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/2f77d8056bd608c0d5a285dfff68fefa82f02487) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

I pushed a correction to this PR: 462355ea ("Count the attention sink once per query row in CP p2p") and aa5a1771 (tests).

The earlier version was wrong. cuDNN counts the sink as one more softmax column, so it is included in every p2p tile's softmax stats. Passing the offset to every tile made the LSE merge count the sink once per tile that a query row visits. I also claimed that every rank already holds the full sink gradient. That is not true for p2p, where each rank computes only its own query rows. Without a mask at cp=2, the two errors cancel, which is what my original check measured. Under a causal mask they don't.

The sink now goes only to the local KV tile (step 0), and the sink gradient is all-reduced over the CP group to match a2a. The CP test now covers p2p for learnable and off-by-one softmax. It also fixes an aliased reference that made the sink-gradient check compare the CP result with itself. I updated the description with the cross-node GH200 results, and the updated test fails on the previous head.

There is one open question at the end of the description, about whether every CP rank should return the full sink gradient (the current a2a contract) or only its partial sum.

I pushed 2f77d805 ("Support FP8 attention with a sink in CP p2p") and updated the description with B300 (sm_103) results.

With a sink, the FP8 per-tile forward returns the offset as a third aux tensor. The FP8 branch unpacked exactly two entries, so I had kept FP8 + sink + p2p off FusedAttention. On B300 the FP8 cases fail with "too many values to unpack" when only that gate is removed. With the unpacking fixed they pass: delayed, current and MXFP8 scaling, sbhd and thd. So the commit fixes the unpacking and drops the gate.

The B300 runs also cover cases the GH200 runs did not:
- p2p with thd, on cuDNN 9.27
- BF16 and FP16 across all three layouts
- a2a with the new non-zero offsets, including the sliding-window config and FP8
- cp=4 on four GPUs

All pass. The previous head fails the sink-gradient check at cp=4 as well.

The question about the per-rank sink-gradient contract at the end of the description is still open.
